title: NoHo Jun 2023 14.jpg
author: Epicgenius
changes: perspective-corrected crop of three window-pair bays of one storey (pairs 2, 3 and 4 of the front; six different photographed windows), resampled once from the original (Catmull-Rom; x reduced about 2.5x with 3x supersampling, y enlarged about 1.85x because one storey has to fill 2048 px); four-corner straightening refined from the measured jambs and string courses; bays on an even 682.67 px grid by a piecewise-linear x map through the measured bay centres (real pitch differs by under 0.1 per cent); y mapped linearly between the undersides of the two string courses; brick courses levelled once, gently, by a smooth displacement field measured from the bed joints (range -6 to +11 panel px, about half that in source px; residual about 1.5 px). The panel's top and bottom edge is the shadow line under the string course (dark to dark), not a cut through brick. THREE local interventions, all in or beside the pier that wraps from pair 4 round to pair 2: (1) the photo's edges slant inwards towards the bottom, so in that pier the brick is stretched sideways from about row 1300 downwards: 3 per cent at row 1400, 11 per cent at row 1660, 20 per cent at the foot of the brick, 25 per cent in the dark mouldings of the string course; nothing above row 1300 is stretched; (2) the real brickwork right of pair 4's right-hand window (jamb quoins and pier) has one course fewer between the shoulder block and the base block than the rest of the wall, so it could not meet the other side of the pier course for course: that zone (from the opening edge outwards) is shifted vertically by up to 36 px so its bed joints follow the wall's courses (its courses come out about 4 per cent lower), and ONE of its courses (a plain course between two quoin teeth, about 36 px tall) is repeated near the foot, at panel rows about 1527-1600; (3) the two halves of that pier (one continued from pair 4, one continued leftwards from pair 2) are joined course by course with a hard switch at the best-matching column, after matching their brick tone. Slow tone evened on the buff brick only, zero-mean so nothing is brightened (under 6 per cent); light unsharp mask (sigma 1 px, 0.3). No denoising, no blur, no recolouring, nothing painted; no pixel comes from outside the photo.
building: Schermerhorn Building, 376-380 Lafayette Street at Great Jones Street, NoHo, Manhattan; Henry J. Hardenbergh, 1888-89; Lafayette Street front, fifth storey, second to fourth window pairs counted from the Great Jones Street corner: paired one-over-one sash windows in buff/salmon brick, each pair under a two-piece red sandstone lintel with stone shoulder blocks, stone base blocks, a red moulded-brick centre pier with stone cap and base, toothed red-brick jamb quoins, on a continuous moulded string course with tile flashing
